Seven is Duō Tóngfǔ.
Eight is Shímó.
Nine is Nóngxiě.
Ten is Liánghuǒ.
Eleven is Huīhé.
Twelve is Tiěwán.
Thirteen is Jīnfǔ.
Fourteen is Cháiláng.
Fifteen is Jiànshù.
Sixteen is Hánbīng.
The sentient beings within them
grow iron claws on their hands and are mutually angry and enraged.
They seize each other with their claws, and their flesh immediately drops off.
They perceive (xiǎng) themselves as dead.
Furthermore, the sentient beings within hold thoughts of malicious harm.
They hold swords and knives in their hands and hack and stab each other repeatedly.
Their bodies are peeled, sliced, cut, and shattered onto the ground.
They perceive themselves as dead.
When a cold wind blows, they instantly revive and stand up.
They say to each other, "I am now alive."
Having suffered the sin for a long time, they exit Xiǎng Dìyù.
Panicked and seeking salvation, they unknowingly suddenly arrive at Hēishā Dìyù.
Hot winds violently arise, blowing hot black sand to adhere to their bodies.
The skin is burned through to the bone, and flames erupt from within the body.
The flames revolve around their bodies, burning and roasting them into decay.
Since their sins are not yet finished, they are made not to die.
Having suffered the pain for a long time, they exit Hēishā Yù and arrive at Fèishǐ Yù.
Boiling excrement and iron balls naturally fill the front area.
The sinful beings are driven and forced to embrace the iron balls, which burn their bodies and hands.
They are further forced to put them into their mouths.
Passing down from the throat to the abdomen, nothing is left uncharred and rotten.
There are iron-beaked insects (tiěchǐ chóng) that chew the flesh down to the marrow, causing measureless suffering and pain.
Since their suffering for sins is not yet complete, they refuse to die again.
Having suffered the pain for a long time, they exit Fèishǐ Yù and arrive at Tiědīng Yù.
Wardens abruptly throw them down onto hot iron.
They stretch out their bodies and use nails to pin their hands and feet.
Five hundred nails cover the entirety of their bodies.
Suffering extreme agony and wailing, they still do not die.
Having suffered the pain for a long time, they exit Tiědīng Yù and arrive at Jī'è Yù.
They are immediately thrown onto hot iron, and molten copper is poured into their mouths.
Passing down from the throat to the abdomen, nothing is left uncharred and rotten.
Since the remaining sins are not finished, they still do not die.
Having suffered the pain for a long time, they exit Jī Dìyù and arrive at Kě Dìyù.
They are immediately thrown onto hot iron, and hot iron balls are placed in their mouths.
Burning their lips and tongue, passing all the way down, nothing is left uncharred, rotten, agonizing, and weeping.

Having suffered the pain for a long time, they exit Kě Dìyù and arrive at Yī Tóngfǔ Dìyù. The hell wardens glare angrily, grab the feet of the sinful beings, and throw them upside down into the cauldron (fǔ).
Following the surging boil of the liquid, they spin up and down.
Their bodies are ruined, rotten, and cooked; ten thousand poisons arrive simultaneously, causing them not to die.
Having suffered the pain for a long time, they exit Yī Tóngfǔ and go to Duō Tóngfǔ Dìyù.
They seize the feet of the sinful beings and throw them upside down into the cauldron.
Following the surging boil of the liquid, they spin up and down, and their whole bodies are ruined and rotten.
They are taken out with iron hooks and placed into other cauldrons.
Their sorrowful cries and bitter agony cause them not to die.
Having suffered the pain for a long time, they exit Duō Tóngfǔ and go to Shímó Dìyù.
They grab those sinful beings and throw them onto a hot stone.
They stretch out their hands and feet and use a great hot stone to crush (kuò) their bodies.
It revolves, rubbing and grinding their bones and flesh into paste.
The bitter agony and acute pain cause them not to die.
Having suffered the pain for a long time, they exit Shímó Yù and go to Nóngxiě Dìyù.
Pus and blood boil up, and the sinful beings run wildly east and west within it.
Their bodies are scalded, and their heads and faces are ruined and rotten.
They are also forced to take the pus and blood and eat it.
Passing all the way down, the bitter, unbearable pain causes them not to die.
Having suffered the pain for a long time, they then exit Nóngxiě and go to Liánghuǒ Dìyù.
There is a great heap of fire whose flames are intensely blazing, and the sinful beings are driven and forced.
They hold an iron measure (shēng) in their hands to measure the heap of fire.
The entire body is burned, suffering bitter, painful heat.
Moaning, groaning, wailing, and weeping cause them not to die.
Having suffered the pain for a long time, they exit Liánghuǒ Yù and arrive at Huīhé Dìyù.
It is five hundred yojanas (yóuxún) wide, long, deep, and shallow in all directions.
Ashy liquid boils up, foul gases rise in billows, and circling waves clash, producing a dreadful sound.
From the bottom to the top, iron thorns cross horizontally and vertically.
On the banks of the river, there is a forest of Sword Trees (Jiànshù Lín).
The branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits are all knives and swords.
The sinful beings enter the river, rising and falling with the waves.
They turn over and sink; the iron thorns pierce their bodies.
Pierced inside and out, pus and blood flow out.
Suffering ten thousand kinds of agony causes them not to die.
When they exit the Ash River and reach the opposite bank,
sharp swords cut and stab their bodies, wounding and breaking them.
Furthermore, jackals and wolves (cháiláng) come and gnaw the sinful beings, eating their flesh raw.
They run up the Sword Tree, where the sword blades face downward.
When they descend the Sword Tree, the sword blades face upward.
When they climb with their hands, their hands are severed; when they step with their feet, their feet are cut off.
Skin and flesh drop off, leaving only white bones connected by sinews.
At that time, there are iron-beaked crows (tiězuǐ wū) on the Sword Tree.
They peck their heads and eat their brains; the bitter agony and screaming cause them not to die.
They return to the Ash River, sinking and drowning with the waves.
Iron thorns pierce their bodies, causing ten thousand kinds of bitter agony.
Skin and flesh are rotten and ruined, and pus and blood flow out.
Only white bones float exposed.
When a cold wind blows, they instantly stand up.
Drawn by past karma, they unknowingly suddenly arrive at Tiěwán Dìyù.
There are hot iron balls, and the hell ghosts (yùguǐ) drive and throw them.
Hands and feet are rotten and ruined, and the entire body is set ablaze.
Ten thousand poisons arrive simultaneously, causing them not to die.
Having suffered the pain for a long time, they then exit Tiěwán and go to Jīnfǔ Dìyù.
They grab these sinful beings and throw them onto hot iron.
They use hot iron adzes and axes (jīnfǔ) to chop their hands, feet, ears, noses, and bodies.
The bitter agony and screaming still cause them not to die.
Having suffered the sin for a long time, they exit Jīnfǔ Yù and go to Cháiláng Dìyù.
There is a pack of jackals and wolves competing to rush forward and gnaw them.
Flesh falls off, bones are injured, and pus and blood flow out.
Ten thousand kinds of pain cause them not to die.
Having suffered the pain for a long time, they then exit Cháiláng and go to Jiànshù Yù.
When they enter that Sword Forest (Jiàn Lín), violent winds arise.
They blow the leaves of the Sword Trees onto their bodies.
Their heads, faces, and bodies are all wounded and ruined.
There are iron-beaked crows (tiězuǐ wū) that peck out their two eyes.
The bitter pain and mournful wailing cause them not to die.
Having suffered the pain for a long time, they then exit Jiànshù and go to Hánbīng Yù.
A great cold wind blows upon their bodies.
Their entire bodies are frostbitten, and skin and flesh drop off.
Suffering agony and screaming, they finally die.
Those whose bodies were unwholesome, and whose mouths and minds were likewise [unwholesome],
fall into Xiǎng Dìyù, horrified until their hair stands on end.
The Hēi Shéng Dà Dìyù.
There are sixteen small hells surrounding it.
Each is five hundred *yóuxún* (yojanas) in length and breadth.
Why is it named Black Rope (Hēi Shéng)?
The various jailers seize the sinners and throw them onto hot iron.
They stretch out their bodies and use hot iron ropes to fasten them straight.
They use hot iron axes, following the path of the ropes, to chop the sinners into hundreds and thousands of pieces.
Furthermore, they fasten them with iron ropes and saw them.
Furthermore, countless hot iron ropes are hung crosswise.
They drive the sinners to walk between the ropes.
Violent, evil winds suddenly arise, blowing the iron ropes across their bodies.
They burn the skin, penetrate the flesh, scorch the bones, and boil the marrow—suffering and agony in ten thousand forms.
Because their remaining sins are not yet exhausted, they are made not to die.
Thus, it is named Hēi Shéng.
After enduring suffering for a long time, they exit Hēi Shéng and arrive at the Hēi Shā Dìyù (Black Sand Hell).
Then, proceeding until the Hán Bīng Dìyù (Cold Ice Hell), they finally perish.
Those who bear malicious intent toward their parents, the Buddha, or the Śrāvakas,
then fall into the Hēi Shéng Yù; their suffering is immeasurable.
The Tuī Kuài Dà Dìyù (Crushing and Grinding Great Hell).
There are sixteen small hells surrounding it.
Each is five hundred *yóuxún* in length and breadth.
Why is it named Crushing and Grinding (Tuī Kuài)?
There are great stone mountains, two mountains facing each other.
When a person enters here,
the mountains naturally close, crushing and grinding their body.
Their bones and flesh are pulverized, and the mountains return to their original places.
Suffering and agony in ten thousand forms—thus they are made not to die.
Furthermore, there are great iron elephants whose entire bodies are ablaze, roaring as they come.
They trample and kick the sinners, who writhe upon them.
Their bodies are pulverized, and pus and blood flow out.
They wail and cry mournfully, yet they are made not to die.
Again, they seize the sinners, lay them on great stones, and crush them with great stones.
Again, they take the sinners, lay them on the ground, and pound them with iron pestles.
From foot to head, their skin and flesh are pulverized.
Pus and blood flow out, and ten thousand agonies arrive simultaneously.
Because their remaining sins are not yet exhausted, they are kept from dying; thus, it is named Tuī Kuài.
After enduring suffering for a long time, they exit Tuī Kuài and arrive at Hēi Shā Dìyù.
Then, proceeding until the Cold Ice, they finally perish.
Those who merely commit the Three Evil Deeds and do not practice the Three Good Conducts,
fall into the Tuī Kuài Dìyù; their suffering is immeasurable.
The Jiàohuàn Dà Dìyù (Wailing Great Hell).
There are sixteen small hells.
Each is five hundred *yóuxún* in length and breadth.
Why is it named Wailing Hell (Jiàohuàn Yù)?
The jailers seize the sinners and throw them into great cauldrons.
They also place them inside great iron boilers.
Hot water surges and boils, cooking those sinners.
They wail and scream; the pain is bitter and searing.
Furthermore, they take those sinners and throw them onto iron griddles.
They fry and roast them back and forth, wailing and screaming.
Because their remaining sins are not yet exhausted, they are made not to die; thus, it is named Jiàohuàn.
After enduring suffering for a long time, they exit Jiàohuàn and arrive at Hēi Shā Dìyù.
Then, proceeding until the Cold Water, they finally perish.
Those who harbor malice and hatred and commit various evil deeds
fall into the Jiàohuàn Dìyù.
The Dà Jiàohuàn Dà Dìyù (Great Wailing Great Hell).
There are sixteen small hells.
Why is it named Great Wailing (Dà Jiàohuàn)?
They take the sinners and place them into great iron vats.
They also place them into iron cauldrons.
Hot water surges and boils, cooking those sinners.
They also throw them onto great iron griddles.
They fry and roast them back and forth, wailing and crying loudly; the pain is bitter and searing.
Because their remaining sins are not yet exhausted, they are made not to die; thus, it is named Dà Jiàohuàn.
After enduring suffering for a long time, they exit Dà Jiàohuàn and arrive at Hán Bīng Yù.
Then they finally perish.
Those who habitually adopt various wrong views,
who are drawn by the net of attachment,
and commit despicable acts
fall into the Dà Jiàohuàn Yù.
Shāozhì Dìyù (Burning and Roasting Hell).
There are sixteen small hells.
Why is it named Burning and Roasting (Shāozhì)?
They lead the sinners and place them inside iron cities.
The cities are burning; they are red both inside and outside, burning and roasting the sinners.
They are also placed upon iron towers.
The towers are burning; they are red both inside and outside.
They are also thrown into great iron furnaces.
The furnaces are burning; they are red both inside and outside.
Burning and roasting the sinners until their skin and flesh are scorched and rotten, ten thousand agonies arriving simultaneously.
Because their remaining sins are not yet exhausted, they are made not to die.
Thus, it is named Shāozhì.
After enduring suffering for a long time, they exit the Shāozhì Yù and arrive at Hēi Shā Yù.
Then, proceeding until the Cold Ice, they finally perish.
Those who commit acts of burning and roasting fall into the Shāozhì Dìyù.
For long nights, they endure the suffering of burning and roasting.
The Dà Shāozhì Dìyù (Great Burning and Roasting Hell).
There are sixteen small hells.
Five hundred *yóuxún* in length and breadth.
They lead the sinners and place them inside iron cities.
The cities are burning; they are red both inside and outside.
Burning and roasting the sinners until their skin and flesh are scorched and rotten, ten thousand agonies arriving simultaneously.
There are great fire pits where the flames rage intensely.
On both banks of the pits are great fire mountains.
They seize the sinners, impale them upon iron pitchforks, set them upright in the fire, and intensely burn and roast them until their skin and flesh are scorched and rotten.
Because their remaining sins are not yet exhausted, they are made not to die.
After enduring suffering for a long time, they exit Dà Shāozhì and arrive at Hēi Shā Dìyù.
Then, proceeding until the Cold Ice, they finally perish.
Those who abandon the karma of good deeds and commit various evil acts
fall into the Dà Shāozhì Yù.
The Wújiàn Dà Dìyù (Avīci Great Hell / Uninterrupted Great Hell).
There are sixteen small hells.
Each is five hundred *yóuxún* in length and breadth.
They seize the sinners and peel off their skin from foot to crown.
Then they wrap the skin around the sinners' bodies.
They place them beneath fiery cartwheels, rolling them over the hot iron ground.
Moving back and forth, their bodies are smashed and macerated.
Skin and flesh fall off, and ten thousand agonies arrive simultaneously; thus, they are made not to die.
Furthermore, there is an iron city where fire arises on four sides.
Flames from the east reach the west, and flames from the west reach the east.
North and south, above and below, it is also like this.
The raging flames circle wildly; there is no empty space between them.
They run east and west, burning and roasting their bodies until the skin and flesh are scorched and rotten.
Bitter and searing pain; ten thousand agonies arrive simultaneously.
When the sinners have been inside for a long time, the gate finally opens.
The sinners run desperately toward it.
Flames erupt from all the limbs and joints of their bodies.
When they are about to reach the gate, the gate naturally closes.
Because their remaining sins are not yet exhausted, they are made not to die.
Furthermore, the sinners within, wherever they cast their eyes, see only evil forms.
Their ears hear evil sounds, and their noses smell foul odors.
Their bodies encounter painful sensations, and their minds contemplate evil doctrines.
In the space of a finger snap, there is no moment without suffering.
Thus, it is named Wújiàn Dìyù (Uninterrupted Hell).
After enduring suffering for a long time, they perish.
Due to the heavy karma of wicked actions which generates rebirth in the evil destiny.
Then, proceeding until the Hán Bīng Dìyù,
they finally perish.
Those whose heavy karma of wicked actions produces rebirth in the evil destiny,
fall into the Wújiàn Yù; their sin cannot be measured.
Each of the Eight Great Hells has sixteen small hells.
Between the two great Jīngāng mountains,
a great wind arises, named Sēngqū.
If this wind were to come to the Four Continents and the Eighty Thousand Continents,
all the mountains of the Great Earth, even those rising ten *lǐ* (li) from the ground,
or even a hundred *lǐ*, flying high in the air, would all be pulverized
like light husks scattered into the air by a strong man's hand.
It is because of these two great mountains that this wind is blocked and stopped.
If the wind were to reach the Four Continents,
the streams, rivers, great rivers, and oceans of the sentient beings therein would all dry up and wither.
Furthermore, the wind between the mountains is foul, unclean, putrid, filthy, and intensely virulent.
If it were to come to the Four Continents,
the smoke would cause all sentient beings to lose their eyesight.
Moreover, these two mountains provide many benefits.
This is also brought about by the karmic retribution of sentient beings' actions.
Furthermore, between the two mountains, there are ten Hells (Dìyù).
The first name is Hòuyún.
The second name is Wúyún.
The third name is Hēhē.
The fourth name is Nàihé.
The fifth name is Yángmíng.
The sixth name is Xūgāndí.
The seventh name is Yōubōluó.
The eighth name is Jūwùtóu.
The ninth name is Fèntuólì.
The tenth name is Bōtóumó.
Why is it called Hòuyún?
The sinners in this Hell spontaneously generate bodies.
They are like thick clouds, hence the name Hòuyún.
Why is it called Wúyún?
The bodies of sentient beings born there are like lumps of flesh, hence the name Wúyún.
Why is it called Hēhē?
The suffering and pain penetrate the body, and everyone cries out "Hēhē," hence the name Hēhē.
Why is it called Nàihé?
The sentient beings undergoing punishment suffer bitter, piercing pain, having no refuge, and all cry out "Nàihé."
Why is it called Yángmíng?

The sentient beings undergoing punishment suffer pain that pierces the body; they wish to raise their voices and speak, but their tongues cannot turn, sounding exactly like the bleating of sheep (Yángmíng).
Why is it called the Xūgāndí Flower?
The Hell is entirely black, like the color of the Xūgāndí Flower.
Why is it called the Yōubōluó Flower?
The Hell is entirely blue-green, like the Yōubōluó Flower.
Why is it called the Jūwùtóu Flower?
The Hell is entirely crimson, like the color of the Jūwùtóu.
Why is it called the Fèntuólì Flower?
The Hell is entirely white, like the Fèntuólì Flower.
Why is it called the Bōtóumó Flower?
The Hell is entirely red, like the color of the Bōtóumó Flower.
The analogy is of a basket holding sixty-four measures (hú) full of sesame seeds.
A person takes away one sesame seed every hundred years.
This continues until they are all gone.
The punishment received in the Hòuyún Dìyù is not yet finished.
Twenty lifetimes in the Hòuyún Dìyù,
is equal to the lifespan of one Wúyún Dìyù.
Twenty lifetimes in the Wúyún Dìyù,
is equal to the lifespan of one Hēhē Dìyù.
Twenty lifetimes in the Hēhē Dìyù,
is equal to the lifespan of one Nàihé Dìyù.
Twenty lifetimes in the Nàihé Dìyù,
is equal to the lifespan of one Yángmíng Dìyù.
Twenty lifetimes in the Yángmíng Dìyù,
is equal to the lifespan of one Xūgāndí Dìyù.
Twenty lifetimes in the Xūgāndí Dìyù,
is equal to the lifespan of one Yōubōluó Dìyù.
Twenty lifetimes in the Yōubōluó Dìyù,
is equal to the lifespan of one Jūwùtóu Dìyù.
Twenty lifetimes in the Jūwùtóu Dìyù,
is equal to the lifespan of one Fèntuólì Dìyù.
Twenty lifetimes in the Fèntuólì Dìyù,
is equal to the lifespan of one Bōtóumó Dìyù.
Twenty lifetimes of Bōtóumó Dìyù is called one Intermediate Kalpa (Zhōngjié).
Twenty Intermediate Kalpas is called one Great Kalpa (Dàjié).
In the Bōtóumó Dìyù, the flames are intensely blazing.
Sinners are one hundred Yóuxún away from the fire.
At sixty Yóuxún away, the fire already scorches them.
At this point, both ears are deaf and cannot hear anything.
At fifty Yóuxún away, both eyes are blind and can see nothing further.
Bǐqiū Qúbōlì had already conceived wicked thoughts.
He slandered Shèlìfú and Mùjiànlián.
When his body disintegrated and his life ended, he fell into this Bōtóumó Dìyù.
The Ābí Dìyù is eight thousand Yóuxún in length, breadth, and height.
It has seven layers of iron city walls and seven layers of iron netting.
Below, there are eighteen sections (gé).
The entire circumference has seven layers.
All of them are Forests of Knives (Dāolín).
Furthermore, there are seven layers of Forests of Swords (Jiànlín).
At the four corners, there are four great bronze dogs.
They are forty Yóuxún long and wide.
Their eyes are like flashes of lightning.
Their tusks are like Sword Trees (Jiànshù).
Their teeth are like Mountains of Knives (Dāoshān).
Their tongues are like iron thorns.
All the hairs on their bodies are ablaze with fierce fire.
The smoke smells foul.
There are eighteen prison wardens (Yùzú).
Their mouths are like those of Yakṣas (Yèchā).
Sixty-four eyes scatter and burst forth iron balls.
The dogs' fangs stick upwards, four Yóuxún high.
Fire streams from the tips of the fangs, burning and roasting iron chariots.
The wheel nets emit fire.
Sharp blades, swords, and halberds burn the city of Ābí, making it red like molten copper.
The Yùzú have eight heads and sixty horns.
The horns scoop up and ignite fire.
The fire transforms into copper, then transforms again into wheels of knives (Dāolún).
They follow one after another in the midst of the flames.
Filling the city of Ābí.
Inside the city, there are seven iron pillars.
Fire surges like boiling iron, melting and bursting forth from the four gates.
Above, there are eighteen cauldrons.
Boiling copper overflows and floods throughout the city.
Between the two sections, there are eighty-four thousand large iron pythons and snakes.
They spit venom into the fire, and their bodies fill the city.
These snakes roar like heavenly thunder.
They rain down five hundred great iron balls.
Furthermore, there are five hundred million insects.
Eighty-four thousand mouths stream fire, descending like rain.
Filling the city of Ābí.
When these insects descend, the fierce fire intensely blazes, illuminating the area above the Hell for eighty-four thousand Yóuxún.
It rushes into the great ocean, scorches the mountains, penetrates the bottom of the great ocean, and the drops are as large as chariot axles.
If there are those who murder their father, harm their mother, or curse and insult their immediate family (liùqīn),
at the time of their death, the bronze dogs transform into eighteen chariots.
Their appearance is like jeweled canopies (bǎogài).
All the flames transform into jade maidens (yùnǚ).
The sinners see this from afar, their hearts rejoice, and they desire to go.
When the Wind Blades (Fēngdāo) slice their bodies, they feel an urgent cold and lose their voice.
They wish they could obtain a good fire, place it on the chariot, ignite it, and self-immolate.
Immediately, their lives end.
They sit on the golden chariots and gaze at the jade maidens.
All (the maidens) grasp iron axes and chop and sever their bodies.
In the time it takes to bend and stretch an arm, they fall straight into Ābí.
From the upper section, they spiral down like spinning wheels of fire until they reach the bottom section.
Their bodies fill the inside of the section.
The bronze dogs roar loudly, chewing the bones and sucking the marrow.
The Yùzú and Luóchà grab great axes and cut them; they use forks to stab their necks and make them stand up, their entire bodies enveloped in flames filling the Ābí Dìyù.
Yánluó Wáng loudly announces and commands:
"Foolish person! Seed of Hell!
When you were in the world,
you were unfilial to your parents, arrogant, and without principle.
The place where you are now born is named Ābí Dìyù."
The Yùzú then carry them from the lower section back up to the upper section.
They pass through eighty-four thousand sections, their bodies snagged as they go, until they reach the edge of the iron net.
One day and one night (in Ābí) is sixty Minor Kalpas (Xiǎojié) in Yánfútí.
The entire duration is one Great Kalpa (Dàjié).
Those who commit the Five Heinous Crimes (Wǔ Nì Zuì).
At the time of their death,
the eighteen Wind Blades, like iron fire-chariots, dismember and sever their bodies.
Because of the oppression of the heat, they speak these words:
"If only I could obtain beautiful flowers and large, cool trees and play beneath them! Wouldn't that be joyful?"
When this thought arises, eighty-four thousand wicked Sword Forests,
transform into jeweled trees, with flourishing flowers and fruits, lined up before them.
The extremely hot flames transform into lotus flowers.
The sinners rush quicker than a sudden downpour to sit upon the fiery lotus flowers.
Iron-mouthed insects emerge from the fiery flowers, pierce the bones, enter the body, and cause agitation.
All the branches of swords,
shave away the flesh and bone.
Innumerable Forests of Knives descend from above.
Fire chariots, blazing furnaces, and the eighteen kinds of suffering come simultaneously to greet them.
When these phenomena appear, they sink and fall into the ground.
From the lower section upwards, their bodies spread out like flowers, completely filling the lowest section, where the fire blazes fiercely.
Reaching the upper section, their bodies fill it entirely.
Because the burning distress is so urgent, they open their eyes and stick out their tongues.
Tens of billions of molten copper streams and hundreds of thousands of knife wheels,
descend from the sky, entering at the neck and exiting at the feet.
All these sufferings exceed those previously mentioned by hundreds of thousands or millions of times.
Those who commit the Five Heinous Crimes receive punishment for five kalpas.
Furthermore, there are sentient beings
who violate the Four Parājikas (Sì Chóng Jìn), falsely consume charitable offerings (xìnshī), spread slander, hold erroneous views (xiéjiàn), and fail to recognize cause and effect (yīnguǒ).
They interrupt the study of Bōrě and destroy the Buddhas (Fó) of the ten directions.
They steal Sēngqí property, are lewd and licentious, and lack principle.
They coerce nuns (ní) of pure precepts, sisters, and close relatives.
They commit various evil deeds.
The retribution for the crimes of these people is this:
At the moment of death,
the Wind Blades sever the body; they lie down restlessly as if being scourged.
Their minds become confused and chaotic, giving rise to wild, deluded thoughts.
They see their own houses, and all the men, women, and children,
as being entirely impure things.
Feces and urine, stinking and putrid, overflow and stream outside.
The Yùzú and Luóchà lift them up with large iron forks.
The Ābí Dìyù and the various Forests of Knives,
transform into jeweled trees and cool, clear ponds.
The flames transform into golden-leafed lotus flowers; the iron-mouthed insects transform into wild ducks and geese.
The sound of suffering and pain is like singing and chanting.
The sinner hears this and thinks, "I shall roam within it."
They sit upon the fiery lotus flower.
The myriad things fiercely tear them apart.
Dogs devour their heart.
In a brief instant,
their body, like an iron flower, completely fills the eighteen sections.
These sinners endure eighty-four thousand Great Kalpas.
They then enter the eighteen sections in the Eastern direction.
They suffer pain as before.
The Southern, Western, and Northern directions are also like this.
Those who slander the Vaipulya Sūtras (Fāngděng Jīng),
commit the Five Heinous Crimes,
destroy the Sēngqí,
defile Bǐqiūní (nuns),
and cut off all roots of goodness (shàngēn).
Those who commit all these crimes have their bodies fill the Ābí Dìyù.
Their four limbs furthermore fill the eighteen sections.
This Ābí Dìyù only burns sentient beings who are the seeds of such hells.
When the kalpa is about to end, the East Gate immediately opens.
Outside the East Gate, they see
clear springs, flowing water, and forests of flowering fruit trees, all appearing simultaneously.
These sinners see from the lower section that the bright fire temporarily ceases.
They rise from the lower section, writhing and crawling on their bellies.
Dragging their bodies, they run up to the upper section.
They climb by grasping the wheels of knives.
At that moment, hot iron balls rain down from the empty sky.
They run toward the East Gate, and upon reaching the threshold,
the Yùzú and Luóchà, holding iron forks, stab their eyes inversely.
Iron dogs bite their hearts, and they faint and die.
The Southern, Western, and Northern Gates are also like this.
They endure for half a kalpa.
There are eighteen minor hells.
The minor hells
each possess eighteen Cold Hells (Hán Dìyù),
eighteen Dark Hells (Hēi'àn Dìyù),
eighteen Minor Hot Hells (Xiǎo Rè Dìyù),
eighteen Knife Wheel Hells (Dāo Lún Dìyù),
eighteen Sword Wheel Hells (Jiàn Lún Dìyù),
eighteen Fire Cart Hells (Huǒ Chē Dìyù),
eighteen Boiling Excrement Hells (Fèi Shǐ Dìyù),
eighteen Cauldron of Boiling Water Hells (Huò Tāng Dìyù),
eighteen River of Ash Hells (Huī Hé Dìyù),
fifty billion Sword Forest Hells (Jiàn Lín Dìyù),
fifty billion Thorn Forest Hells (Cì Lín Dìyù),
fifty billion Copper Pillar Hells (Tóng Zhù Dìyù),
fifty billion Iron Jī Hells (Tiě Jī Dìyù),
fifty billion Iron Wheel Rim Hells (Tiě Wǎng Dìyù),
eighteen Iron Cave Hells (Tiě Kū Dìyù),
eighteen Iron Ball Hells (Tiě Wán Dìyù),
eighteen Sharp Stone Hells (Jiān Shí Dìyù),
eighteen Molten Copper Drinking Hells (Yǐn Tóng Dìyù).
Hells as numerous as these.
In the Ābí Dìyù,
having died, they are reborn amidst cold ice.
Having died in the Cold Ice Hell, they are reborn in a dark place.
For eighty million years, their eyes see nothing.
They take the body of a large insect, wriggling and crawling on its belly.
Their senses are blocked by darkness, and they are eaten by foxes and wolves.
Afterwards, they are reborn as animals (Chùshēng).
For fifty million lifetimes, they take the forms of birds and beasts.
They return to be reborn among humans.
Their six senses are incomplete; they are poor and humble.
After five hundred lifetimes, they are reborn as starving ghosts (Èguǐ).
Thereafter, they meet a compassionate teacher (Shàn Zhīshì) and generate the aspiration for enlightenment (Pútí Xīn).
Regarding the eighteen Cold Hells (Hán Dìyù):
There are ice mountains in the eight directions.
The mountains are divided into eighteen sections.
Furthermore, there are eighteen small ice mountains.
The cold ice mountains resemble tiled lotus flowers in the gaps between them.
They are eighteen Yóuxún high.
Above them are ice wheels.
Their vertical and horizontal dimensions are exactly twelve Yóuxún.
Like hailstones falling from the sky,
they rob, plunder, steal, strip, freeze, and kill living beings.
When the karmic retribution for this person is about to reach the end of life,
all the knife winds transform into searing fire.
The sinner thinks, "Why am I not lying upon the ice now?"
As this thought arises,
the jailers, the Ràchàsa, holding ice wheels, arrive swiftly through the void.
When the sinner sees them, their heart immediately desires the ice.
Their breath ceases, their life ends, and they are reborn on the ice mountains.
Immediately after birth,
the eighteen ice mountains seem to fan them.
All the cold ice enters through their pores.
Filling every space among the eighteen sections.
They are split, cracked, and ripped apart like a red lotus flower.
Ice wheels cover their bodies, both above and below.
The ice mountains in the eight directions close in simultaneously.
They speak no other words, only crying, "Āluō!"
At that time, the sinner immediately thinks,
"When shall I escape this cold ice and be reborn amidst the searing fire?"
At that time, there is an iron-beaked bird in the sky.
It spits fire, breaking the ice and pecking at the brain.
The sinner dies instantly.
The jailers strike the ground again with an iron pitchfork and shout, "Live! Live!"
Responding to the sound, they immediately revive.
The fire in their body rages fiercely, and they wish to obtain the ice from before to extinguish this fire.
The jailers again greet them with the ice wheels and place them in the hell.
Thus, there is no one who does not pass through all eighteen sections.
The lifespan in this Cold Hell
is eighty million years, like the months and years of the Cāturmahārājika Deva (Sì Tiānwáng Tiān).
When the penalty is finished, they are reborn as humble, poor, and lowly beings.
For fifty lifetimes, they are slaves and maidservants.
Their clothes do not cover their forms, and their food does not fill their mouths.
After this karma is finished,
they meet a Shàn Zhīshì and generate the Pútí Xīn.
Regarding the Dark Hells (Hēi'àn Dìyù):
eighteen layers of dark mountains,
eighteen layers of dark nets,
eighteen layers of iron beds,
eighteen layers of iron shrouds.
One mountain is eighty-four thousand Yóuxún high.
Each shroud is also eighty-four thousand Yóuxún thick.
Between each shroud are eighteen layers of iron mountains, with Ràchàsa as numerous as a forest.
These mountains are dark and shadowy.
[Those reborn here are those who] stole the lamps and light of the Buddha and the Sangha (Sēng).
Who stole from their parents, teachers (shī), and elders (zhǎng).
Who slandered those who preached the Dharma.
And who also destroyed secular masters (shī) of argument and debate.
They did not respect the distinguished or the lowly, nor did they know shame (cánkuì).
Because of this sin, when they are about to die,
electric light flashes in their eyes, rapidly and continuously.
They immediately think,
"What sin have I committed that I constantly see this fire?"
They immediately close both eyes, wishing not to see.
When their life is about to end,
the jailers, the Ràchàsa, lift a large iron bed and spread out a great iron wheel.
Like a great gathering cloud,
they arrive through the sky.
They are formless but have sound.
The sinner, wanting to depart and die,
sits upon the iron bed and falls into the dark place.
Knife wheels above and below cut and sever their body.
There are large iron crows whose beaks and claws are long and sharp.
They fly down from the mountain and tear at the sinner.
In extreme pain, they run quickly, seeking light but finding none.
Caltrops beneath their feet pierce through bone to the marrow.
They wander terrified like this for five million billion years, their time calculated as before.
That person strikes their head against all the dark mountains.
Brain matter flows out, and eyes pop out.
The jailers, the Ràchàsa, stab with iron pitchforks and place the eyes back into the sockets.
When the karma is finished, they are released.
They become poor people.
Their eyes are crossed, blind, dark, and unable to see.
Or they are driven away by lepers.
They endure this karmic retribution for five hundred lifetimes.
After this is past, they meet a Shàn Zhīshì and generate the Pútí Xīn.
Regarding the eighteen Minor Hot Hells (Xiǎo Rè Dìyù):
They are like the Ābí Dìyù.
They also have seven surrounding walls and seven layers of iron wheel rims (Tiě Wǎng).
Innumerable evils adorn them.
[Those reborn here are those who] did not follow the teacher's instructions and developed a wicked, rebellious mind.
Who ignored kindness and nurture, stole from the teacher (shī), and harmed the teacher.
Who defiled the teacher's pure food, sat on the teacher's bed or seat, seized the teacher's alms bowl (bō yú), or hid things away uncleanly.
Who made various wicked poisons and gave them to the teacher to drink.
Or Śramaṇa (Shāméng) or Brāhmaṇa (Póluómén).
Who committed all sorts of illegal acts without shame (cánkuì).
Who stripped statues, destroyed stūpas (tǎ), or plundered the Dharma treasures.
Who murdered uncles, aunts, parents, brothers, or sisters.
When their life is about to end,
the eighteen jailers each use an iron pitchfork to hold and place them in a section of the hell.
Like a great jeweled canopy raining down fine, subtle drops.
The raindrops, resembling flowers, enter the heart as burning anguish.
Seeing the rain as cool and refreshing, they immediately think and say,
"I wish I could sit under the shade of that canopy."
"Wouldn't it be joyful for the cool rain to sprinkle upon me?"
Their breath ceases, and their life ends.
In the blink of an eye, they are sitting atop the Sword Forest (Jiàn Lín).
Billions of sword blades.
All the blades emit fire, burning and stabbing their body.
The jeweled canopy in the sky transforms into a wheel of fire.
It descends from above, splitting their skull directly.
Their body shatters into several thousand pieces.
Copper balls rain down from above and enter through their pores.
The jailers, the Ràchàsa, stab the sinner's eyes with large iron pitchforks.
Or they shoot iron arrows that pierce their heart, causing them to faint and die.
After a moment, they revive, sitting on the sword bed.
A fierce whirlwind blows them down into the hell.
Then Yánluó Wáng (Yama) announces,
"Offspring of the hells, you committed many evils."
"You killed teachers (shī) and slandered teachers."
"The place where you are now reborn is called the Tongue-Plucking Ābí."
"You must remain in this hell for three kalpas (jié)."
Having spoken these words, he immediately disappears.
Regarding the Knife Wheel Hells (Dāo Lún Dìyù):
Knife Mountains (Dāo Shān) stand on four sides.
Knives are piled up like wheels between the various mountains.
There are eight million billion extremely large knife wheels.
They descend in sequence, like drops of rain.
[Those reborn here are those who] enjoyed inflicting pain on others and killed living beings.
When their life ends,
they suffer from a choking illness, and their heart is hard as stone.
They immediately make this wish:
"Wouldn't it be wonderful to obtain a sharp knife to cut away these various afflictions?"
At this time, the jailers bear the knife wheels on their heads, causing them to appear obscured (or momentarily invisible).
They come to the sinner and speak humble and modest words,
"I have sharp knives that can cut away severe illnesses."
The sinner rejoices and immediately thinks to themselves,
"Only this will bring relief."
Their breath ceases, their life ends, and they are reborn upon the knife wheels.
Like a drunken elephant running and falling into the gap between the Knife Mountains.
At that time, the four mountains close in simultaneously.
The four kinds of Knife Mountains cut and slice their body.
Unable to bear the suffering, they faint and die.
The jailers, the Ràchàsa, drive and push the sinner.
Forcing them to climb the Knife Mountain and reach the summit.
The knives injure them from the soles of their feet all the way to their heart.
Fearing the jailers, they crawl upward.
Having reached the summit,
the jailers hold all sorts of tree leaves (or branches) in their hands.
Before they die, iron dogs bite their heart, inflicting a hundred kinds of painful poison.
Iron worms consume and eat their flesh entirely.
Immediately, they shout, "Live!"
Iron wheels are attached to their feet, and they descend from the sky.
In one day and one night, they are reborn six billion times and die six billion times.
The multitude of years is eighty million years, like the lifespan of the Cāturmahārājika Deva.
When the karma is finished, they exit and fall into the animal realm (Chùshēng).
For five hundred lifetimes, they feed the mouths of the multitude.
For another five hundred lifetimes, they take humble forms.
Afterwards, they meet a Shàn Zhīshì and generate the Pútí Xīn.
The *Jiànlún* (Sword Wheel) hell.
Its length and breadth are equally fifty *yóuxún*.
It is filled with sword trees, the number of which is
like rice stalks, hemp, bamboo, and reeds.
Each sword tree is forty *yóuxún* high.
Eighty-four thousand sword wheels serve as leaves.
Eighty-four thousand sword wheels serve as flowers.
Eighty-four thousand sword wheels serve as fruit.
Eighty-four thousand segments of boiling copper serve as branches.
Due to the endless delight in killing,
when such a sinner is approaching death,
they encounter a great fever and immediately think,
“My body is now alternately hot and cold.
My entire body is hard and strong, like an iron anvil.”
They immediately make this wish:
“If only I could get a diamond sword to cut away this suffering—the joy would be unspeakable!”
At that moment, the hell wardens immediately transform themselves
into the form of the person’s own parents or close friends,
appear before the person, and say to them,
“I have a secret method, exactly as you wished for. I should bestow it upon you.”
The sinner says, “Quickly, quickly, I want to obtain it!”
When their breath ceases and life ends, they rush like a horse and are born amidst the sword flowers.
Innumerable swords and knives shave their bones and tear their flesh, scattering it into the air.
Furthermore, there are iron crows.
They descend from the trees, pluck out the eyes, and peck the ears.
There are great *Luóchà* (Rākṣasas).
They hold iron axes, break open the head, and pull out the brains.
Iron dogs come and lick them. After dying, they are shouted back to life.
They are driven to climb the trees.
Before reaching the treetop, their bodies are pulverized like dust.
In one day and one night, the number of times they are killed and turned to dust is countless.
Due to the sin of killing, they suffer such calamity for eighty thousand billions of years, and then are born among the animals.
Their bodies constantly carry heavy loads, and upon death, their skin is peeled off.
After five hundred lifetimes, they are reborn among humans.
They are poor, short-lived, sickly, and emaciated.
After this period, they meet a Good Friend (*Shàn Zhīshì*) and generate the mind of *Pútí* (Bodhi).
The *Huǒchē* (Fire Chariot) hell.
Each copper cauldron,
is forty *yóuxún* in length and breadth equally.
It is filled with fire.
Below, there are twelve wheels.
Above, there are nine thousand and four fire wheels.
Some sentient beings, who were disciples of the Buddha,
and those who served the ninety-six types of *Fàntiān* (Brahma heaven) practices,
and householders who deceived and misled others, living by wrong livelihood, flattering, twisting the truth, and committing evil.
When such a sinner is about to die,
the wind element stirs first, and their body becomes cold like ice.
They immediately think,
“When will I obtain a great mass of raging fire,
if I enter and sit in it, the cold disease will be eternally removed?”
Having had this thought,
the hell wardens (*Luóchà*) transform a fire chariot to look like a golden lotus flower.
The hell wardens on top appear like young boys.
Holding white whisks, they arrive drumming and dancing.
The sinner becomes attached and delighted, thinking,
“If I sit upon this, the pleasure will be unspeakable.”
When their breath ceases and life ends, they are loaded onto the fire chariot.
Their limbs and joints burn, and their body is scorched and scattered.
The hell wardens shout “Live!”, and in response, they revive.
The fire chariot crushes their body eighteen times, shattering it like dust.
Heaven rains boiling copper, sprinkling it over their entire body, and they immediately revive.
Thus they go back and forth, ascending to the edge of the boiling water and falling back into the cauldron.
Crushed by the fire chariot, in one day and one night, they die ninety billion times and are born ninety billion times.
When this person’s sins are exhausted, they are born into a poor and lowly family, and are used by others.
They are bound to others and lack freedom.
After repaying the karmic debt for seeking profit and offerings, they are eventually released.
Due to the merit of their previous compassionate heart from having left home life,
they meet a Good Friend who teaches them the Dharma.
Their mind opens and their intention is realized, and they achieve *Āluóhàn* (Arhatship).
The *Fèishǐ* (Boiling Excrement) hell.
Eighty *yóuxún* large, with eighteen iron cities.
Each iron city has eighteen divisions.
In each division, all four walls have hundreds of billions of sword trees.
The ground is like a knife blade.
The blade is three *chǐ* thick.
Upon the blade are countless hundreds and thousands of caltrops.
Between every caltrop and every sword tree,
innumerable iron worms are generated.
Each iron worm has hundreds of thousands of heads.
Each head has hundreds of thousands of mouths.
At the tip of every mouth, there are hundreds of thousands of serpent-like worms (*yuánchóng*).
These serpent-like worms spit out hot excrement,
boiling like melted copper, filling the iron enclosure.
Above are iron nets and iron crows.
This is for those who broke the eight precepts and fasting,
defiled *Shāmíní* (Śrāmaṇerikā) and *Shìchāmóní* (Śikṣamāṇā),
defiled the precepts of *Bǐqiū* (Bhikṣu) and *Bǐqiūní* (Bhikṣuṇī),
defiled the precepts of *Yōupósè* (Upāsaka) and *Yōupóyí* (Upāsikā).
The above seven assemblies and all others,
who defiled the pure food of the monastic community, or defiled the food of their parents,
stole food, ate it first, or handled it with impure hands,
and monastic administrators (*sēng zhīshì*) who, relying on their authority, defiled the pure food of the monastic community,
or disciples of the four assemblies who, with impure bodies, sat on beds belonging to the monastic community,
or committed *Tōulánzhē* (Sthūlātyaya) and failed to repent for a long time,
or consumed monastic food in vain, or sat among the monastic assembly and performed the *Bùsà* (Upavasatha) ritual.
All such numerous sinners with immeasurable impure and evil karma,
when approaching death, their entire body becomes fragrant.
The smell is unbearable, like a musk deer.
They immediately think,
“Where can I go where I won't smell this fragrance?”
The hell wardens transform themselves, appearing like painted vases filled with filthy excrement.
They approach the sinner and touch them with their hands.
This causes the sinner’s heart to generate love and attachment (for the filth).
When their breath ceases and life ends, they fall into the boiling excrement.
Their body rots away, and the multitude of worms gnaws and eats, shaving the bone down to the marrow.
Driven by intense thirst, they drink the hot boiling excrement.
The serpent-like worms and maggots gnaw at the root of their tongue.
In one day and one night, they are born ninety billion times and die ninety billion times.
When their sins are exhausted, they are born into a poor and lowly family, lacking freedom.
If they are born into the world, they constantly encounter evil kings and belong to masters holding wrong views (*xiéjiàn*).
Various evil deeds oppress their body.
Goiters, swelling, and foul sores serve as their clothing.
Due to the good karma established by hearing the Dharma in previous lives,
they meet a Good Friend, leave home life to study the path, and achieve *Āluóhàn*.
The *Shíbā Huòtāng* (Eighteen Cauldrons of Boiling Water) hell.
There are eighteen cauldrons.
Each is forty *yóuxún* in length and breadth equally.
Seven layers of iron nets contain boiling iron within.
Five hundred *Luóchà* fan great stone coals,
to burn the copper cauldrons, with flames following one another.
For sixty days, the fire cannot be extinguished.
In *Yánfútí* (Jambudvīpa), this equals twelve myriad years.
The boiling cauldron water surges upward, transforming into fire wheels,
which return and fall back into the cauldron.
This is for those who destroyed the Buddha’s prohibitions and precepts, and killed living beings for sacrificial rituals,
burned mountains and wildernesses to eat meat, thereby harming sentient beings,
or ate living beings raw, or burned them with fire.
When such a sinner is about to die,
their body and mind are distressed, and they lose control of urination and defecation.
They are either hot like boiling water or cold like ice.
They immediately think,
“Wouldn’t it be delightful to get large warm water and enter it for a bath?”
The hell wardens (*Luóchà*) transform themselves into servants.
Holding basins of hot water, they approach the sinner.
The sinner’s heart generates love and pleasure.
When their breath ceases and life ends, they are born inside the boiling cauldrons.
They rapidly melt and rot away, leaving only the bones behind.
Iron forks haul them out, and iron dogs swallow them.
They vomit them onto the ground, and immediately they revive.
The hell wardens drive and pursue them, forcing them back into the cauldrons.
Because the iron cauldrons are hot, they climb the sword trees.
Their bones and flesh break apart and fall into the boiling cauldron water.
In one day and one night, the cycles of death and life are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges (*Héngshā*).
When the sins are exhausted, they are born as pigs, sheep, chickens, and dogs.
There is no short-lived state that they do not experience.
They undergo rebirth in this way for eighty million years.
After their life ends, they are reborn among humans.
They receive two types of retribution:
First, being sickly;
Second, being short-lived.
After immeasurable *jié* (kalpas), they meet a Good Friend.
They accept and uphold the five precepts and practice the Six *Bōluómì* (Pāramitās).
The *Huīhé* (Ash River) hell.
It is two hundred *yóuxún* long.
It is twelve *yóuxún* wide.
Below are sharp knives, and on the banks are sword trees.
It is filled with raging fire, twelve *zhàng* wide.
Furthermore, there is melted ash covering the fire.
Forty *zhàng* thick.
This is for those who stole from their parents, teachers, good friends, brothers, or sisters.
Such foolish people have no shame or remorse.
They do not recognize benevolence and nurture, nor do they follow the teacher’s instructions.
When the life of such a person, bearing such karmic retribution, is about to end,
gas fills their heart and abdomen, and their breathing is intermittent.
They immediately think,
“My heart is like mud, and air fills my chest.
Wouldn’t it be pleasant if I could get a faint fire to explode my body?”
The hell wardens, responding to this thought, transform into the sinner's wife and children.
Holding fire censers covered with faint ash,
they approach the sinner.
The sinner rejoices.
When their breath ceases and life ends, they are born inside the Ash River.
Among the sword trees, there is a *Luóchà*.
Holding a sharp sword, intending to cause harm, the person is terrified and runs into the Ash River.
As they raise their feet and put them down, knives wound their legs.
The sword trees rain knives, which penetrate through their pores.
A *Luóchà* uses a fork to pierce out their heart.
They collapse to the ground, faint and die, but immediately revive.
In one day and one night, they are born five hundred billion times and die five hundred billion times.
Driven by hunger and thirst, they open their mouth wanting to eat.
The sword trees rain knives which enter through the tip of the tongue.
They tear open the abdomen and split the chest, fainting and dying.
Due to the merit of having heard the Dharma and the name of the *Sēng* (Saṅgha) in a previous life,
after their sins are exhausted, they are reborn among humans.
They are poor and lowly.
Realizing the impermanence of the world, they leave home life to study the path.
If there is no Buddha in the world at that time, they achieve *Pìzhīfó* (Pratyekabuddha).
If there is a Buddha in the world, they achieve *Āluóhàn*.
Regarding the Hell of the Forest of Swords (Jiàn Lín Dì Yù):
Eight thousand *yóu xún* (yojanas) are filled with sword trees.
There are hot iron balls serving as their fruits.
The trees are twenty-four *yóu xún* tall.
Due to being unfilial to parents and disrespectful to teachers and elders.
Committing the karma of harsh speech, lacking compassion, and assaulting people with knives and staves.
When nearing the end of life, the mind is like sticky glue, generating attachments everywhere.
They immediately produce this thought:
“My mind is bound and attached, unwilling to give up anything it touches.”
“Indulging in wine and craving sex, though meeting suffering, my heart still does not cease.”
“If I could get a sharp knife, I would sever this craving.”
The jailers (yù zú) respond to the sound and transform into attendants.
Holding a mirror, they speak:
“Your heart has many attachments; you may observe this mirror.”
They see the image of a sharp sword.
They then immediately form this thought:
“My body is frail and weak, unable to endure the affairs of desire.”
“If I obtain this sharp sword,”
“to sever my heart, would this not be delightful?”
As this thought arises, their breath stops, life ends, and they receive the body of a hungry ghost (è guǐ).
Among the sword trees, iron balls spontaneously generate.
Entering from the crown, they exit, burning and rotting the intestines and abdomen.
The jailers beat and drive them, forcing them to climb the trees.
Iron-beaked insects devour them, terrifying them onto the trees.
Thus revolving, they pass through the entire Forest of Swords.
In one day and one night, they undergo eighty thousand births and deaths.
After the karma is completed, they are born in ages of famine and kalpas of sickness (jí bìng jié).
As humans, they are lowly and despised; their breath is constantly foul, and people hate the sight of them.
Later, they meet a spiritual friend (shàn zhī shí) and develop the thought of enlightenment (pú tí xīn).
Regarding the Hell of the Forest of Thorns (Cì Lín Dì Yù):
Eight thousand *yóu xún* are filled with iron thorns.
On the tip of every single thorn, there are twelve swords.
Furthermore, on the trees are large hot iron hooks.
Due to harsh speech, double-tongued speech, flowery speech, and unjust speech.
Teasing excessively, and deceitfully spreading slander and gossip.
Speaking faults about the Sūtras and classics, and slandering masters of commentarial literature.
As retribution for such sins, when their life is about to end, their throat is parched and their tongue is dry.
They immediately produce this thought:
“If I could get a sharp thorn to pierce my neck and draw blood,”
“causing water to flow through my veins, would that not be delightful?”
The jailers (yù zú) and Rākṣasas (Luó Chà) transform into their parents, holding bright pearls.
Thorns grow on the top of the pearls, which they hold near the mouth, as if water is about to drip.
The sinner rejoices, their breath stops, and life ends.
In the space of a lightning flash, they are born amidst the Forest of Thorns.
The jailers and Rākṣasas hold iron hooks and pull their tongues out.
Eight thousand iron oxen, with large iron plows, plow and tear their tongues.
In one day and one night, they undergo six hundred births and deaths.
After this has passed, they are born among humans.
Their shoulders are narrow, their faces wrinkled, and their speech stammering and halting.
Such sinners have sores growing on their bodies.
Pus and blood overflow, and for five hundred lifetimes, people hate the sight of them.
After this has passed, even if they speak, people do not believe or accept it.
They meet a spiritual friend (shàn zhī shí) and develop the thought of enlightenment (pú tí xīn).
Regarding the Hell of the Copper Pillar (Tóng Zhù Dì Yù):
There is a forest of copper pillars, like a volcano.
It is six hundred *yóu xún* high.
Below there is raging fire; above the fire is an iron bed, and above that are wheels of knives.
Interspersed are iron-beaked insects and iron-mouthed crows.
Due to proliferating confusion from greed, and defiled love and impurity.
Performing impure deeds in improper places and at improper times.
Suppose there are Bhikṣuṇīs (Bǐ Qiū Ní), Brahmans (Pó Luó Mén), and other practitioners of pure conduct (fàn xíng zhě).
If they violate the purity laws at improper times or in improper places.
This includes all who commit perverse conduct (xié xíng zhě).
When such sinners are nearing the end of their lives,
their whole body becomes stiff, shaking and unsteady.
They immediately produce this thought:
“If I could get a sturdy, large copper or iron pillar,”
“to bind this body so that it does not shake.”
The jailers instantly transform into servants.
Holding iron staves in their hands, they come to the sinner.
They report, saying, “Elder (Zhǎng Zhě),”
“Your body is now stiff, and other objects are weak; you may grasp this staff.”
Their heart immediately rejoices, their breath stops, and life ends.
In the time it takes to brandish a staff, they are born on top of the copper pillar.
The raging flames intensely burn their bodies.
Frightened, they look down and see on the iron bed
a beautiful woman.
If it is a woman, she sees a handsome man.
Love and attachment arise in their hearts, and they throw themselves down from the copper pillar to the ground.
The copper pillar pierces their body, an iron net binds their neck, and iron-beaked insects devour their body.
They fall onto the iron bed.
Both men and women simultaneously feel fire rising from the six sense organs.
Iron-beaked insects enter through the eyes and exit through the sexual organs.
For those who violate the precepts, there are separately nine hundred million small insects.
Like maggots, they have twelve beaks.
Fire emerges from the tips of the beaks, devouring their bodies.
In one day and one night, they undergo nine hundred million births and nine hundred million deaths.
They are born in the bodies of doves and pigeons for five hundred lifetimes.
They are further born among the Nāgas (lóng) for five hundred bodies.
Afterward, they are born among humans as those lacking roots (wú gēn), having dual roots (èr gēn),
or having uncertain roots, or the bodies of eunuchs (huáng mén) for five hundred lifetimes.
Even if they manage to be born human,
their wives are not chaste, their children are not kind or filial, and their servants are disobedient.
After this has passed, they meet a spiritual friend (shàn zhī shí) and develop the thought of enlightenment (pú tí xīn).
Regarding the Hell of the Iron Loom (Tiě Jī Dì Yù): there is an iron bed.
Its length and width are exactly four hundred *yóu xún*.
Various levers are installed on top.
Between the levers are ten thousand million iron crossbows.
The iron crossbows, pot-shaped heads, and a hundred million sharp blades.
Because of greed and desire, they are unfilial to their parents.
They are disrespectful to teachers and elders.
They do not follow good teachings and kill sentient beings.
When this person’s life ends, their body shakes violently, and fluids flow from the six apertures.
They see their own bed as soft as *dōu luó mián* (cotton/kapok).
“Would it not be delightful to lie down in a firm, cool place?”
The jailers and Rākṣasas (Luó Chà),
lift the bed with forks, melting the fire mats, and arrive at the sinner’s location.
They joyfully wish to lie down.
Their breath stops, life ends, and they are born on the iron loom.
Ten thousand million iron levers are fastened and moved from below; the iron levers rise up boundlessly.
The iron crossbows simultaneously extend two iron (devices/arrows).
Arrows shoot into the sinner's heart.
In one day and one night, they undergo six hundred million births and deaths.
Afterward, they are born among animals (xù shēng) for five hundred lifetimes.
They return to be born among humans.
They are poor and lowly, employed by others.
They often fall into prisons and constantly suffer beatings.
Later, they meet a spiritual friend (shàn zhī shí) and develop the thought of enlightenment (pú tí xīn).
Regarding the Hell of the Iron Net (Tiě Wǎng Dì Yù):
Eighty-nine layers of iron nets (luó wǎng).
Between every single net are a hundred million iron needles.
Each iron needle is equipped with five fastened levers.
Due to perverse thoughts, flattery, and bewitching people with seductive charms.
Harboring slanderous and harmful intentions, and evil thoughts day and night.
When nearing the end of life, their body itches intensely.
They immediately produce this thought:
“If I could get a bundle of needles and stab myself, would that not be delightful?”
As this thought arises, the jailers transform into skilled physicians.
Holding sharp needles in their hands, they announce:
“To cure the sickness.”
The sinner’s heart rejoices, their breath stops, life ends, and they are born amidst the iron nets.
As they struggle downward, all the levers move.
Countless needles shoot into their pores.
Thus, they twist and turn among the iron nets.
In the space of a *chà nà* (ksana), they die and are born again.
Only after the karma is finished are they born in remote lands where the Buddha Dharma (Fó Fǎ) does not exist.
They do not even hear the teaching of worldly good words, much less the Right Dharma (Zhèng Fǎ).
Although born among humans, they are classified as being in the three evil paths.
Later, they meet a spiritual friend (shàn zhī shí), but although they hear the Dharma, their mind does not understand it clearly.
Regarding the Hell of the Iron Cave (Tiě Kū Dì Yù):
This is the supreme suffering among the paths of hungry ghosts (è guǐ dào).
There is an iron mountain.
Its length and width are exactly twenty-five *yóu xún*.
On the mountain, there are also five hundred million million large hot iron balls.
Every single iron ball is perfectly round, measuring thirteen *yóu xún*.
Among the mountain ranges, there are also hundreds and thousands of knives and swords.
At that time, a small hole opens on the east side of that mountain.
It is like a *mó jiā tuó shēng* (Magadha measure), but only black smoke emerges.
Due to the bondage of stinginess and greed, their heart is like a diamond (jīn gāng).
They only enjoy seeking and acquiring, never being satisfied.
They give nothing to their parents, wives, or children.
They regard the instructions of teachers and elders as filthy refuse.
They do not give clothes or food to servants, maids, relatives, or friends.
Such a stingy person does not contemplate impermanence (wú cháng).
They protect and treasure wealth as if it were their eyes.
When life is about to end, all senses are blocked.
Their mouth is shut, they do not speak, and they silently think in their heart:
“After I die, these wicked people”
“will eat my wealth as if swallowing iron balls.”
“Living in my cave-dwelling will be like dwelling in a dark room.”
Having formed this thought,
the jailers transform into a stingy person.
They gather much wealth and burn it with fire.
The sinner’s heart rejoices, their breath stops, life ends, and they are born on top of the volcano.
They are like molten copper poured into the iron cave.
Sword-worms and knife-worms devour their bodies.
Smoke blinds their eyes, and they cannot see the flames.
Running wildly east and west, their heads strike the iron mountain.
Iron balls pass through them from the crown to the foot.
In the space of a single thought (yī niàn), they die and are born again.
Only after the karma is finished are they born among hungry ghosts (è guǐ).
Their body grows to several tens of *yóu xún* in height.
Their throat is like a needle tube, and their belly is like a great mountain.
As they seek food east and west, molten copper is poured into their throat.
This lasts for eight thousand years.
They are born among the ghosts who eat pus, saliva, and blood.
They are further born among lavatory deities (cè shén), pigs, dogs, and the like.
Only after the karma is finished are they born in places of poverty, lowliness, and lack of clothes or food.
They meet a spiritual friend (shàn zhī shí) and develop the thought of enlightenment (pú tí xīn).
The Hell of Iron Pellets (Tiěwán Dìyù) is this:
eighty *yóujùn* full of iron cities.
Eighty-eight sections.
In each section there are five mountains of knives.
They are used to cover the top.
Below are eighteen large, wicked iron snakes.
All spew iron swords, the tips of the swords burning with fire.
(This is for those who) destroy and insult acts of giving, saying that giving yields no recompense,
and encourage people to hoard and accumulate.
They speak to kings, high officials, *Shāmén*, *Póluómén*, and all beings,
saying that giving has no cause and no fruit of retribution.
When this person is near death, their neck stiffens and their pulse shrinks.
They turn away, remain silent, and dislike seeing people.
They lie down, looking downwards, only thinking in their heart:
"The treasures I accumulated
will accompany me, and the joy is unspeakable."
The hell wardens transform into his wife, holding hot iron pellets.
They transform the pellets into a precious vessel before the person.
They say:
"I will follow you in death, clinging intimately, never to be separated."
When breath ceases and life ends, they are born inside the iron city, running east and west.
The iron snakes release poison, wrapping around their body, and fire burns at every joint.
Immediately they have this thought:
"May the heavens love me and pour down sweet rain."
Corresponding to this thought, great hot iron pellets rain down, entering through the neck and exiting through the feet.
After the retribution for the offense is finished, they are born as poor, solitary, mute people.
The number of years is as stated in the description of the Iron Cave (Tiěkūe).
They meet a good spiritual advisor (*shàn zhīshì*) and arouse the thought of enlightenment (*pútíxīn*).
The Hell of Pointed Stones (Jiānshí Dìyù) is this:
There are twenty-five stone mountains.
On each stone mountain there are eight water pools.
In each water pool there are five poisonous dragons.
(*Bǐqiū*, monks) and (*Bǐqiūní*, nuns),
(*Shāmí*, novice monks) and (*Shāmíní*, novice nuns),
(*Shīchāmóní*, probationary nuns),
(*Yōupósè*, laymen) and (*Yōupóyí*, laywomen),
and practitioners of the ninety-five kinds of *Fànzhì* (Brahmin) laws, etc.
If they violate minor precepts,
and do not repent for a long time, having no shame or remorse in their hearts.
When life is about to end,
the region below the heart is full of gas, the belly swells like a drum.
Food causes choking and vomiting, and liquid cannot pass down.
Immediately they have this thought:
"Wouldn't it be wonderful to get a pointed stone to plug my throat?"
At that time, the hell wardens transform into skillful physicians.
They grasp and twist pointed stones, making large pills and placing them in the person's mouth.
They command them, "Close your mouth."
Joy arises in the person's heart.
When breath ceases and life ends, they are born among the stone mountains.
Innumerable pointed stones enter through the back and exit through the chest.
The hell wardens also use iron forks to pry open the mouth and push stones inside.
In one day and one night, this happens sixty billion times.
This is retribution received during life.
When life ends here, they fall into the Hell of Black Ropes (Hēishéng Dìyù).
The Hell of Black Ropes is this:
eight hundred iron chains and eight hundred iron mountains.
Large iron pillars are erected with chains tied to both ends.
The hell wardens rush them, forcing the greedy ones to walk on the iron ropes.
If they cannot maintain their balance, they fall down into a cauldron of boiling soup.
They rush up, desperately thirsty, drinking molten iron and swallowing stones as they run.
In one day and one night, they undergo this suffering a total of a hundred thousand times.
When the retribution for the offense is finished, they are born into the world as servants.
They meet a good spiritual advisor (*shàn zhīshì*) who teaches them the true Dharma.
They attain *Āluóhàn*.
The Hell of Drinking Copper (Yǐntóng Dìyù) is this:
one thousand two hundred kinds of copper chariots of various colors.
On each copper chariot there are six thousand copper pellets.
(This is for those who commit sins) through stinginess, greed, jealousy, wrong views, and wicked speech.
They give nothing to their parents, wife, children, relatives, or anyone else.
Stinginess and jealousy arise in their hearts; seeing others gain profit is like an arrow piercing the heart.
When such a sinner is about to die,
they are often sick, emaciated, delirious, and speak confusedly.
At this time, the hell wardens transform, carrying fruit in a copper chariot and bringing it to the sinner.
Upon receiving it, the sinner is happy.
Immediately they think and say:
"Obtaining this delicious fruit truly satisfies my wishes."
When breath ceases and life ends, they are born upon the copper chariot.
Soon after, they are born among the copper mountains.
The copper chariot crushes their neck.
The hell wardens use tongs to pry open their mouth and force them to drink molten copper.
Dazed and collapsing to the ground, they cry out, "Hungry! Hungry!"
Immediately the hell wardens tear their mouth open.
They place copper and iron pellets into the mouth.
They swallow eighteen pellets.
Fire burns at every joint as they run east and west.
After seven days, life ends.
The hell wardens cry out:
"In your previous life,
you practiced flattery, held wrong views, were stingy, greedy, and jealous.
Due to these causes and conditions, you received the retribution of the iron pellets.
Or perhaps you had left home and violated minor precepts.
For a long time, you did not repent and consumed offerings from believers in vain.
Due to these causes and conditions, you consume all these iron pellets.
The retribution for this person's offense is that for hundreds of millions of years, they will not recognize water or grain.
When the suffering of the offense is finished, they return to be born among humans.
For five hundred lifetimes, their speech is halting and stammering, unable to clearly express themselves.
Due to residual habits from past lives (*sùxí*), after eating, they consume clods of earth.
After this, they meet a good spiritual advisor (*shàn zhīshì*) and arouse the thought of enlightenment (*pútíxīn*).
First: Treading underfoot (Jiǎotà).
Those who previously trampled and killed people are now consumed by the hell ghosts.
This lasts for two hundred years.
Second: Knife Mountain (Dāoshān).
Those who previously killed living beings now receive this punishment for two hundred years.
Third: Examination (Shěndì).
Those who angrily cursed people (who were like) birds and beasts.
For five hundred years, iron pestles strike their mouths.
When the offense is finished, they are born with a human head and a bird body.
Their mouth constantly speaks of their offenses.
Fourth: Embracing Knives and Swords (Bàodāojiàn).
Those who violated the precept against sexual misconduct themselves,
and also committed offenses against those who uphold the precepts.
Fifth: Boiling Sand (Fèishā).
Those who previously covered living beings with hot ashes.
Sixth: Boiling Well (Fèijǐng).
The water in the well is constantly boiling.
(This is for those who) with wicked intent, put unclean substances into a well.
When the offense is finished, for a hundred years, they are a toad (*háma*) in a well.
Seventh: Furnace Window Warden (Zàochuāng Yùzú).
People are inverted and put inside the furnace window.
This is for women who, while alive,
used their reflected image (in a mirror) or their clothes to tempt other men.
Eighth: Mute Ghost (Yǎguǐ).
The hell constantly burns iron stamps (*là*) to brand their tongues.
This is for those who, when alive, did not respond when called by their parents or teachers.
After two hundred years, they are born as mute people.
Ninth: Hot Ashes (Rèhuī).
Seven hundred *lǐ* filled with hot ashes.
This is for people who, while alive, aroused sexual desire,
and sought to sleep with chaste women, though they were ultimately unsuccessful.
They receive punishment for two hundred years.
Afterwards, they are born afflicted with sores and fear.
Tenth: Boiling Excrement (Fèishǐ).
Thirty thousand *lǐ* filled with feces and urine.
People are driven into it.
(This is for those who) previously gave people good food,
but angrily said, "It is like eating filth."
They receive punishment for five hundred years as a pig.
Eleventh: Swollen Stench (Pāngchòu).
Two thousand five hundred *lǐ* in extent.
Filled with pus and blood.
This is for people who, while alive, with impure intent, entered the dwelling of a holy person (*shèngrén shì*) and released gas or defiled the place.
They receive punishment for two hundred and forty years.
Afterwards, they are born among the poor and lowly, their bodies constantly smelling foul.
Twelfth: Impurity (Bùjìng).
A thousand *lǐ* in extent, filled with snot and spit.
(This is for those who) with arrogant hearts and unclean hands, crushed incense and made offerings to a Great Sage (*Dàshèng*).
Afterwards, when born among humans, they are always arrogant.
Thirteenth: Impurity (Bùjìng).
Six hundred *lǐ* of pus.
(This is for those who) while alive, in the middle of eating,
had rat droppings or dog scraps, which are unclean,
and threw them into clean food.
They receive punishment for two hundred years and are born as dogs.
Fourteenth: Black Ears, Perpetual Darkness (Hēi’ěr Cháng’àn).
(This is for those who) while alive, with wicked intent, obstructed the Buddha's radiance (*Fó Guāngmíng*).
They receive punishment for seven hundred years.
Fifteenth: Four thousand *lǐ* in extent.
They are constantly chopped, shot, beaten, scraped, pushed, and crushed.
This is for people who, while alive, committed the Five Heinous Crimes (*Wǔ Nì Yè*).
They suffer punishment for periods spanning numerous *jié* (kalpas).
If they transfer among various Hells,
the period of the *jié* is also ten thousand years.
Sixteenth: Mutual Killing (Xiāngshā).
Wives kill husbands, husbands kill wives.
Mothers kill children, children kill mothers.
This person formerly killed the parents of others,
and also killed the parents and children of living beings.
When they are born among humans,
their parents, children, and grandchildren all die prematurely.
Seventeenth: Chopped Body (Zhuóshēn).
They are constantly chopped by the hell ghosts.
This is because they previously chopped living beings.
Afterwards, when born, they frequently encounter legal trouble (*xiànguān*).
Eighteenth: Fire Chariot (Huǒchē).
This person previously burned and killed living beings.
Afterwards, when born, they are afflicted by burns.
Nineteenth: Not Recognizing the Dharma (Bùshífǎ).
Full of ignorant people who hear the sound of the *jiànchuí* (gong/wooden fish),
and arrogantly lie down.
Afterwards, they are born in border regions.
Twentieth: Iron Frying (Tiěáo).
This is for those who fried shrimp and crabs.
Afterwards, when born, they have a short lifespan.
Twenty-one is called the starving ghost (Èguǐ).
Their body is forty lǐ long.
Their belly is like a basket holding ten thousand hú (measures).
Their neck is ten lǐ long.
They constantly suffer from hunger and thirst; their breath is constantly foul.
When they see food, it transforms into charcoal.
Drink becomes pus and blood.
This is for those who ate vegetarian food but did not uphold the fast (zhāi).
Afterwards, they will be reborn for eight hundred generations, constantly acting as a Luóchà.
Twenty-two is called Solid Charcoal (Gāngtàn).
Those who took others' possessions with a thieving mind will hold solid charcoal in their hands.
Afterwards, they are born poor and lowly, serving others.
Twenty-three is called Cauldron of Boiling Water (Huòtāng).
This is for those who, when alive, maliciously poured hot water on earthworms.
Twenty-four is called Iron Bed (Tiěchuáng).
Those who committed adultery with other men's wives or coerced women who upheld the precepts.
Men embrace the copper pillar; women lie upon the iron bed.
Twenty-five is called Iron Pellet (Tiěwán).
This is for those who roasted or boiled chicken or duck eggs.
Afterwards, they will constantly suffer from confusion and dereliction.
Twenty-six is called the Arrogance Sitting Hell (Gònggāo Zuò Dìyù).
This is for those who, when alive, were arrogant and consumed the offerings of the faithful (xìnshī).
They relied on their presumed virtue and aroused a heart of arrogance.
Twenty-seven is called Black Ears (Hēi'ěr).
The hell guardians dismember them limb by limb with knives.
This is for those who committed adultery with Bhikkhus (Bǐqiū).
Afterwards, they are born among the low and base women.
For five hundred years, they will be eunuchs (huángmén).
Twenty-eight is called Cold Ice Hell (Hánbīng Yù).
This is for those who, when alive, threw living beings into cold and freezing places.
Afterwards, they are born poor and lowly, constantly without clothes.
Twenty-nine is called Stone Cave (Shíkū).
It is filled with smoke and fire.
This is for those who maliciously fumigated and killed living beings.
Thirty is called Provisional Detention (Quánshōu).
The hell guardians detain them for maliciously extinguishing dust and killing nits and lice with a heart of hatred.
Thirty-one is called Cuò.
This is for those who used a tool to crush (cuò) nits and lice.
Afterwards, they are born with a short lifespan.
Thirty-two is called Hot Water Poured on the Body (Rètāng Jiāoshēn).
This is for those who wore fine clothing to lure other men’s wives.
When the crime is concluded, they become birds and beasts.
Thirty-three is called Starving Ghost (Èguǐ).
Their body is thirty lǐ long.
Below their throat, they have a goiter; they pierce it and eat the pus.
Sometimes they see good food.
The multitude of ghosts compete to seize it, and they cannot eat it.
This is for those who obtained good food from others but did not first offer it to the senior practitioners (shàngzuò).
Afterwards, they are born poor.
Thirty-four is called Starving Ghost (Èguǐ).
Their body is ten lǐ or five lǐ long.
Their body hair is sharp and rigid.
This is for those who were stingy, did not offer food, and claimed they had nothing when they truly did.
Afterwards, they are born poor and lowly, mostly lacking food and drink.
Thirty-five is called Vicious Dogs (Ègǒu).
There are many vicious dogs whose teeth are sharp as swords.
The hell guardians summon the dogs, which compete to bite them.
This is for those who, when alive, summoned dogs to bite and kill living beings.
Afterwards, if they are reborn as a person, they enjoy being bitten by dogs.
Thirty-six is called Iron Stakes (Tiěyì).
People are driven to step upon them.
This is for those who, when alive, looked at their parents, teachers, and elders with venomous intent.
Afterwards, they are born among venomous snakes.
Thirty-seven is called Skin Peeling (Bōpí).
Ghosts constantly use sharp knives to peel off their skin.
This is for those who maliciously stripped off other people's clothes or bedding.
Or stripped the hides of living beings.
Afterwards, if they are born among humans, they are constantly robbed and deprived by others.
Thirty-eight is called Hanging Upside Down (Dàoxuán).
The jailers seize people and hang them upside down.
This is for those who, when alive, hung living beings upside down.
Thirty-nine is called Animal Birth (Chùshēng).
The hell guardians pour molten copper into their mouths.
This is for those who incurred debts, denied them, and did not repay them.
Afterwards, for five hundred years,
they will be cattle, horses, slaves, or servants for humans.
They will enjoy being whipped and beaten.
Forty is called Ploughing the Body (Gēngshēn).
The hell guardians plough their bodies with iron ploughs.
This is for those who, when alive, ploughed the ground, injuring living beings.
(And) maliciously cursed.
Forty-one is called Piercing the Eyes (Zúyǎn).
The hell guardians constantly use iron arrowheads to pierce their eyes.
