This is for those who, when alive, looked at their parents with malicious intent and evil eyes.
Afterwards, if they are born among humans, their eyes constantly have exposed pupils.
Forty-two is called Weapons (Dāobīng).
The hell guardians chop and shoot them.
This is for those who, when alive, killed each other with a heart of hatred.
Afterwards, if they are born among humans, they enjoy being chopped and shot.
Forty-three is called Cutting and Stabbing (Gēcì).
The hell guardians cut off their flesh while they are alive.
This is for those who, when alive, maliciously cut off human flesh.
When the crime is concluded, if they are reborn as a person, they enjoy being cut and stabbed.
Forty-four is called Iron Millstone (Tiěmó).
The hell guardians grind people with the iron millstone.
This is for those who, when alive, maliciously ground and killed worms inside the mill.
Forty-five is called Bàngnòng.
It is filled with iron millstones.
The hell guardians drive people into the millstones and grind them.
Forty-six is called Bàngnòng.
This is for those who, when alive,
saw living beings enter the grinding device (bàngnòng),
and maliciously swore, "I will not save them."
Afterwards, if they are born among humans, their body is sallow and mature (diseased).
Forty-seven is called Stone Mortar (Shíjiù).
The jailers drive people into the mortar and pound them.
This is for those who, when alive, maliciously pounded and killed living beings.
When the crime is concluded, they become snails or clams (Luóbàng).
Forty-eight is called Arrogance (Jiāomàn).
[The victims have] human heads and snake bodies.
This is for those who, when alive, recited Sūtras (sòngjīng) while lying on the ground.
Forty-nine is called Water Hell (Shuǐ Dìyù).
The water stands still and does not flow.
This is for those who, when alive, forced people into the water, causing them to sink and drown.
Fifty is called Cuān rú.
The hell guardians strike people's heads with stones.
This is for those who, when alive, had an arrogant heart.
They made their parents, teachers, and elders wait.
And caused their children, when born, to speak disrespectfully.
Fifty-one is called Iron Rod (Tiěbàng).
The hell guardians constantly strike their bodies with the iron rod. This is for those who, when alive, maliciously killed nits and lice.
Fifty-two is called Terror (Kǒngbù).
They are constantly terrified by Ox-head Āpáng (Niútóu Āpáng).
This is because they constantly terrified people when alive.
Fifty-three is called Iron Stakes (Tiěyì).
Iron stakes are spread on the bottom of the water.
The hell guardians drive people into the water, piercing their bodies until blood flows.
This is for those who, when alive, out of jealousy, spread stakes to injure others.
Fifty-four is called Drinking Molten Copper (Yǐn Yángtóng).
This is for those who, when alive, arrogantly mocked the speech of their parents, teachers, and elders.
Afterwards, they constantly stammer.
Fifty-five is called Iron Arrowhead (Tiězú).
The hell guardians pierce their eyes with iron arrowheads.
This is for those who, when alive, maliciously jabbed the pupils of living beings.
When the crime is concluded, they become blind people.
Fifty-six is called Iron Fork Hell (Tiěchā Yù).
The hell guardians fork people with iron forks.
This is for those who, when alive, maliciously forked fish and other living beings.
Fifty-seven is called Maggots (Qūchóng).
They suck and eat the person’s body.
This is for those who, when alive, were jealous and harmed people.
and harmed the domestic animals and property.
When the crime is concluded, if they are reborn as a person, their body suffers from malignant sores.
Fifty-eight is called Knives Dismembering Hands (Dāojiě Shǒu).
The hell guardians dismember their two hands with sharp knives.
This is for those who, when alive, with an arrogant heart,
used impure hands to grasp Sūtras (jīng).
Fifty-nine is called Weeping and Crying (Tíkū).
The hell guardians escort them and terrify them, causing them to weep and cry.
This is for those who, when alive, constantly worried about money and wealth to facilitate lustful desires.
Afterwards, if they are reborn as a person, they constantly suffer from lack of wealth.
Sixty is called Iron Shackles (Tiějū).
The hell guardians constantly use iron shackles to restrain their bodies.
This is for those who, when alive, shackled and killed living beings.
Sixty-one is called Molten Copper (Yángtóng).
The hell guardians pour molten copper into their mouths.
This is for those who, when alive, with a malicious heart,
committed false speech (wàngyǔ), double-tongued speech (liǎngshé), wicked cursing (èmà), and flowery speech (qǐyǔ).
When the crime is concluded, if they are reborn as a person, their breath is constantly foul.
Sixty-two is called Molten Copper Poured on Hands (Yángtóng Guàn Shǒu).
This is for those who, when alive, did not respect the Way (Dào) in their hearts.
And grasped the robes of Śrāmaṇas (Shāmén) with impure hands.
Sixty-three is called Shooting the Body (Shè Shēn).
The hell guardians shoot them with arrows.
This is for those who, when alive, maliciously shot and killed living beings.
Sixty-four is called Unrestricted (Wúzé). Generally, there are five Kings:
One is called King Suí (Suíwáng).
Two is called King Jié (Jiéwáng).
Three is called King Chǒu (Chǒuwáng).
Four is called King Zìrán (Zìránwáng).
Five is called King of Living Beings (Zhòngshēngwáng).
All of them generate faith in the Mahāyāna (Dàshèng) vow to save the beings in the hells.
Those whose sins in the various hells are concluded come to enter this place.
Their past conduct and the severity of the sins they committed are judged.
They abandon their hell body and receive the form of an intermediate being (zhōngyīn xíng), like a small child three years old.
Then, following their actions and karma (yè), they receive rebirth from parents.
Huó Dà Dìyù.
Malicious hearts, anger, and contention, stabbing each other with spears.
Iron claws grabbing and snatching, blood staining and flowing widely.
Pain and poison fiercely press, tormented without realization.
Cold wind comes and blows.
The hell guardians call the sinful people "Live!" and they revive.
Therefore, it is named the Huó Dìyù.
The beings within this place, in their former lives, delighted in killing sentient beings: oxen, sheep, birds, and beasts.
For the sake of profits such as fields, residences, territories, and wealth, they mutually killed and harmed.
They receive this karmic retribution.
Héhuì Dà Dìyù.
Ràchà hell guardians.
Taking various forms, [having] heads of various evil beasts,
they come to swallow, devour, bite, and gnaw the sinful people.
Two mountains press together, and hot iron wheels crush [them].
Hot iron mortars pound them, just like pressing oil.
Piles of flesh accumulate, streams of blood form ponds.
Vultures, eagles, tigers, and wolves each come to pull and tear.
These people, in their former lives, frequently killed sentient beings, and they return to suffer in this type of hell.
Furthermore, they used power and influence to bully, push down, and suppress the weak.
They receive the punishment of the two mountains pressing together.
Miserliness, greed, anger, delusion, and fear.
Judging cases light or heavy without righteous principles.
Or destroying the righteous path.
They receive the crushing by hot iron wheels and the pounding by iron mortars.
The fourth and fifth are named Jiàohuàn and Dà Jiàohuàn.
The sinful people within this Great Hell.
The Ràchà hell guardians have yellow necks and red eyes, and fire issues from their mouths.
They wear scarlet clothes, and their body flesh is tough and hard.
They run and shoot the sinful people.
The sinful people, terrified and mad, knock their heads [on the ground], begging for pity.
They call out, "Great General, please show a little compassion!"
They are led into the Hot Iron Hell.
A hundred yóujùn in length and breadth.
They are driven and beaten, driven and run, and their feet are all scorched.
Fat and marrow flow out like oil pressed from herbs.
[Struck] with iron rods on their heads and foreheads, their brains flow out like a broken curd jar.
They are then led into iron enclosures and rooms.
Black smoke comes to suffocate them.
They are piled up and crushed together, intending to seek a way out.
The doors are already closed, and the loud shouts and anguished cries never cease.
These people, in their former lives, cheated with scales and measures.
They judged cases illegally and received deposits but did not return them.
They bullied the inferior and troubled the poor, causing them to wail and cry.
They destroyed others' cities and ravaged human settlements.
They harmed, robbed, and plundered, causing the entire city to shout and scream.
They fraudulently lured people out and then harmed them.
Now they suffer in the Jiàohuàn Dìyù.
They smoked creatures that lived in holes to death, or confined them in prisons.
Or they smoked them to death in dark, smoky caves.
Or they threw people into wells and robbed them of their property.
All receive the karmic retribution of the Dà Jiàohuàn Dìyù.
The sixth and seventh are Rè and Dà Rè Dìyù.
Within them are two large copper cauldrons.
Filled with scalding boiling water.
The Ràchà hell guardians throw the sinful people into them.
Feet up and head down, their bones and joints disintegrate.
They pull them out with a trident, the cold wind revives them, and they are thrown back into a coal pit.
Or placed into boiling ashes.
Taken out of the ashes, they are placed upon hot sand.
They are also scorched and refined by pus and blood.
Taken out of the coal pit, they are thrown onto a flaming bed and forcefully driven to sit.
Fire issues from their eyes, ears, nose, mouth, and all their pores.
These people, in their past lives, tormented their parents, teachers, Shàmén, Póluómén, and all good, virtuous people.
They troubled them and caused their hearts to heat up, and now they receive the retribution of the Rè Dìyù.
Or some, in their former lives, boiled living silkworms to death.
Or boiled and melted pigs and sheep alive.
Or pierced a person's abdomen with wood and roasted them alive.
Or burned mountains and fields, and various settlements, Fótú, jīngshè, and celestial shrines.
Or pushed sentient beings into pits of fire.
Therefore, they are born into this hell.
Āpí Dìyù is four thousand lǐ in length and breadth.
That place is the deepest.
The hell guardians and Ràchà peel the skin from the head down to the feet.
They use five hundred nails to nail the body, like stretching out an ox hide.
Hot iron fire-chariots crush the body.
They are driven into fire pits and made to embrace coal and carry it out.
Sharp knives, swords, and spears fly into their bodies, causing them to become dizzy, faint, withered, and cooked.
Or they tumble and fall, creeping about.
These people's past actions involved committing many great evils.
The five heinous crimes, cutting off the roots of goodness.
Calling Dharma non-Dharma, and non-Dharma Dharma.
Destroying cause and destroying effect, hating and envying virtuous people.
They enter this hell, where the suffering is the most intense.
